Graduate Studies
At LSU, graduate students in Physics & Astronomy pursue research that spans the universe—from
the smallest fundamental particles to the largest cosmic structures. Built around
engaging coursework, close faculty mentorship, and hands-on research, the program
offers opportunities in areas including astrophysics, condensed matter physics, medical
physics, and health physics.
Graduate students join active research groups where curiosity drives discovery and
ideas move freely across physics, astronomy, and interdisciplinary science. Whether
exploring the nature of matter and the cosmos or advancing applications in medicine
and radiation science, students are supported in developing as independent scientists
within a collaborative research environment.

Physics & Astronomy
The graduate program in Physics and Astronomy offers research opportunities in areas
ranging from quantum materials and high-energy physics to astrophysics, and cosmology.
Students work closely with faculty using advanced theory, computation, and instrumentation
to explore fundamental questions and develop innovative technologies.
Research Areas
Medical & Health Physics
The Medical and Health Physics graduate program prepares students for careers in medical
physics, health physics, and radiation science. Students gain hands-on research and
training experience in the safe and effective use of radiation for medicine, industry,
and public health. The program combines advanced coursework with collaborative research
to develop skilled scientists and professionals.
